name: 1.8 V FT232-class USB-serial adapter
spec: FT232 chip, logic level 1.8 V (a jumper on some boards, for example DSD TECH SH-U09C2 - a retailer's claim); an FT232R supports break (KGDB sysrq), a CP2102N does not
serves: phones with the console UART on the USB-C SBU pins (Pixel 2 and family, per the sources)
note: Check the level before connecting: 3.3 V can damage a 1.8 V phone. Variants with other chips are other rows.

name: USB-C passthrough breakout that brings out the SBU pins
spec: USB2 data, CC1/CC2 and SBU1/SBU2 passed through; a stock phone cable lacks the SBU and CC lines and does not work
serves: phones with the console UART on the SBU pins

name: USB-Cereal (google/usb-cereal)
spec: SBU1 = TX, SBU2 = RX, DIP 1.8/3.3 V, orientation-specific, not USB-C compliant; repository archived 2023-01-10; sold soldered by third parties
serves: phones with the console UART on the SBU pins
note: A wrong DIP setting can damage the target; the chip edition matters (FT232R vs CP2102N). Prices go in the lab's base, dated.

name: A phone's console on UART through the USB-C SBU pins
wiring: SBU1 (A8) is the phone's TX into the adapter's RX; SBU2 (B8) the phone's RX from the adapter's TX; ground on A1; 1.8 V; 115200 baud, 8N1; orientation differs between phones. On a Pixel: fastboot oem uart enable (bootloader unlocked), reboot to fastboot; fastboot oem uart disable turns it off. It gives a log only.
serves: Pixel 2 and family; each phone's own base says what is confirmed
note: General from the sources; confirmed on no phone here yet (walleye's base holds the claim and, later, its evidence).
